title: Owls of the Night
summary: How owls use their large eyes, flexible necks, sharp hearing, and silent feathers to hunt at night, and why farmers in Saudi Arabia welcome them.
poll: Owls are the best hunters among all birds.

versions.title: Owls at Night
versions.text:
It is late at night. The sky is dark. A bird sits on a branch. It is an owl!

Most owls sleep in the day. At night, they wake up to hunt. They look for prey. Prey is an animal that is caught for food. Owls eat mice, bugs, and small birds.

An owl has big eyes. They help it see in the dark. But its eyes can not move. So the owl turns its head. It can turn its head very far!

Owls hear well, too. Some can find a mouse by sound. They do not need to see it.

An owl flies with no sound. Its soft feathers help. The mouse does not hear it come. Then the owl grabs it with sharp claws.

Owls gulp small prey whole. They can not use the bones and fur. So the owl spits up a small ball. This ball is a pellet. Kids can look in a pellet. They find what the owl ate!

Owls live in Saudi Arabia, too. They help farms. They eat the mice that eat the crops.

versions.title: Owls of the Night
versions.text:
It is late at night, and the desert sky is dark. A bird sits very still on a palm tree. Its big round eyes shine in the moonlight. It is an owl!

There are about 250 kinds of owls in the world. Most of them sleep during the day and hunt at night. They search for prey, which is an animal that is caught and eaten by another animal. Owls eat mice, rats, insects, lizards, and small birds.

Owls also have amazing hearing. Some owls can find a mouse hiding under leaves just by the sound it makes. They do not even need to see it.

An owl can fly with almost no sound. Its soft feathers have tiny fringes on the edges, and these make the air move quietly. The mouse does not hear the owl coming until the owl grabs it with its sharp claws.

Owls swallow small prey whole. But they can not digest the bones and fur. A few hours later, the owl coughs up a small ball called a pellet. Students can take a pellet apart and find out what the owl ate!

versions.title: Owls of the Night
versions.text:
Late at night, when the desert is dark and quiet, a bird sits still on a palm tree. Its large round eyes shine in the moonlight. It is an owl, and it is ready to hunt.

There are about 250 species of owls in the world. Most of them are nocturnal, which means they sleep during the day and become active at night. Owls hunt mice, rats, insects, lizards, and small birds.

An owl's eyes are enormous, so they collect a lot of light. This helps the owl see in the dark. However, its eyes are shaped like tubes, and they can not move in their sockets. To look around, the owl turns its whole head instead. It can turn its head about three quarters of the way around, because its neck has twice as many bones as ours.

Owls also have excellent hearing. The round face of many owls works like a dish that collects sound and sends it to the ears. Some owls can find a mouse under snow or leaves just by listening.

An owl can fly almost silently. The edges of its wing feathers are soft and fringed, so they quiet the rush of air. The mouse does not hear the owl until it is too late. Then the owl grabs it with its sharp, curved claws, called talons.

Owls usually swallow small prey whole, but they can not digest bones and fur. A few hours later, the owl coughs up a pellet. Scientists study pellets to learn what owls eat.

Barn owls, little owls, and eagle owls all live in Saudi Arabia. Farmers welcome them, because a family of barn owls can eat thousands of rodents in a single year.

versions.title: Owls of the Night
versions.text:
Late at night, when the desert is dark and silent, a bird perches motionless on a palm tree, its enormous round eyes glowing in the moonlight. It is an owl, and it is preparing to hunt.

Scientists have identified approximately 250 species of owls, which live on every continent except Antarctica. Most are nocturnal, sleeping during the day and becoming active after sunset, and they are skilled predators of mice, rats, insects, lizards, and small birds.

An owl's eyes are exceptionally large, so they gather a great deal of light, allowing the owl to see in near darkness. However, its eyes are shaped like tubes and cannot move within their sockets. To look around, the owl rotates its entire head instead, turning it up to about 270 degrees, because its neck contains fourteen vertebrae, twice as many as a human neck.

Owls also possess remarkable hearing. The flat, circular face of many owls, called a facial disc, functions like a dish that collects sound and directs it toward the ears. In barn owls, the ears are asymmetrical, with one higher than the other, so the owl can tell whether a sound comes from above or below. As a result, a barn owl can catch a mouse in complete darkness.

An owl can also fly almost silently, because the edges of its wing feathers are soft and fringed, which reduces the noise of rushing air. The prey rarely detects the owl approaching before it is seized by sharp, curved talons.

Owls usually swallow small prey whole, but they cannot digest bones and fur, so they regurgitate these parts as a compact pellet several hours later. Scientists examine pellets to discover exactly what owls have been eating.

During the day, many owls rest in trees, where the brown and grey patterns of their feathers provide camouflage. Barn owls, little owls, and eagle owls all inhabit Saudi Arabia, and farmers appreciate them because a family of barn owls can consume thousands of rodents in a single year.

Scientists have identified approximately 250 species of owls, which inhabit every continent except Antarctica. Most are nocturnal, resting throughout the day and becoming active after sunset, and they are extraordinarily effective predators of rodents, insects, lizards, and small birds.

An owl's eyes are exceptionally large, so they gather a considerable quantity of light, enabling the owl to see in near darkness. However, its eyes are tubular rather than spherical and cannot move within their sockets. To observe its surroundings, the owl rotates its entire head instead, turning it up to approximately 270 degrees, a flexibility made possible by the fourteen vertebrae in its neck, which is twice the number in a human neck.

Owls also possess extraordinary hearing, since the flattened, circular face of many owls, known as a facial disc, operates like a satellite dish that collects sound and directs it toward the ears. In barn owls, the ears are asymmetrical, with one positioned higher than the other, so the owl can determine whether a sound originates above or below it, so that a barn owl can capture a mouse in absolute darkness.

During the day, many owls rest in trees, where the mottled brown and grey patterns of their feathers provide effective camouflage. questions.stem: How is an owl's way of looking around different from a human's?
options: Humans turn their heads, while owls only move their eyes.
An owl turns its whole head because its tubular eyes cannot move in their sockets.
Humans and owls both have fourteen neck vertebrae.
Owls cannot look behind them at all.

wrong.C: Humans have half as many neck vertebrae as owls.
